errors.english: even in the case of possession
errors.why: ldan pa / ldan pa can here are the Vaiśeṣika saṃyoga / saṃyogin (conjunction, the conjoined) as a type of inferential mark, not 'possession'/'possessor'; the note's 'inherence' is also wrong (inherence is 'du ba, which appears as a separate mark on the next side).

fix.find: even in the case of possession
fix.replace: even in the case of conjunction (saṃyoga)

errors.english: follows it, then the certainty
errors.why: It is the reason's capacity to convey (go bar byed pa nyid) that follows the ascertainment of tādātmya and tadutpatti, not the ascertainment that follows it, as the next sentence (de nges pa'i rjes su mi 'jug) confirms.

note: The argument is followed, but the Vaiśeṣika term saṃyoga is rendered 'possession' throughout, and one dependency is reversed.
A careful rendering of a dense Vinaya passage on when a jñapti-karman counts as performed; the boundary case with Upāli is handled correctly.

errors.english: even if the object of sound is not diverse in nature
errors.why: The subject is conjunction (ldan pa), the referent of the word ['diverse'] (sgra'i yul); 'sound' is wrong, and conjunction is dropped.

fix.find: even if the object of sound is not diverse in nature
fix.replace: even if conjunction, the referent of the word ['diverse'], is not diverse in nature

errors.english: a mere designation cannot be the basis
errors.why: The root line says that [conjunction] is not a basis for mere (metaphorical) designation, as the gloss that follows makes clear; the English makes the designation the subject.

errors.english: because of the (inherence) samavāya of many things in a single object of conjunction in a painting
errors.why: This is ekārthasamavāya, conjunction inhering in one and the same object; 'of many things' is not in the Tibetan, and the technical relation is garbled.

note: The anti-Vaiśeṣika argument about the variegated cognition is generally followed, but several technical points are misparsed.

errors.english: The result, which is not the awareness of the aspect of the object, is indeed the cognition of the object.
errors.why: The Tibetan says the result, being awareness of the object's aspect, is also awareness of the object; the added negation contradicts the doctrine being defended.

fix.find: The result, which is not the awareness of the aspect of the object, is indeed the cognition of the object.
fix.replace: Because the result, the awareness of the aspect of the object, is also the cognition of the object.

errors.english: Even if the self is not the agent, it is established as such because of its influence.
errors.why: bdag nyid is reflexive ('although it [the cognition] is itself not an agent'), not 'the self' (ātman); it is established as such through that [activity of understanding the object].

fix.find: Even if the self is not the agent, it is established as such because of its influence.
fix.replace: Although it is not itself an agent, it is established as such through that [activity].

errors.english: it is established as such because of its influence. Therefore, in the ultimate sense
errors.why: These two lines complete the six-line verse; the English cuts them off as prose and links them to the commentary with an added 'Therefore'.

note: The sākāra pramāṇa/phala argument is mostly sound, but a negation is inserted at a key point and the verse's reflexive 'itself' becomes 'the self'.

errors.english: (Kumarila) [note: refers to the Mimamsa scholar Kumarila Bhatta]
errors.why: Nothing in the Tibetan names Kumārila (gzhon nu ma len); the attribution is conjecture presented as an equivalent.

errors.english: is intended to be the producer of its own aspect
errors.why: mngon par sems pa is the false conceiving (abhimāna) of the separated nature as producing its aspect, not 'intended'; the following 'nothing other than what is intended' should be 'nothing other than this conceiving'.

note: Dream/waking validity and the non-observation passage are rendered acceptably; there is an unsupported attribution and one key term blurred.

errors.english: Because his words are encountered by noble beings, they are like those of a high-born person.
errors.why: skyes here is 'gift': when he meets noble people his words become like a gift (welcome); there is no 'high-born person'.

fix.find: Because his words are encountered by noble beings, they are like those of a high-born person.
fix.replace: Because when he meets noble people his words become like a gift,

note: The compound analyses of the verse commentary are paraphrased but sound, except for a misreading of skyes in the opening gloss.

errors.english: Because it is accepted that the cause of attachment arises within the mental continuum, your example is invalid.
errors.why: Continuing from the previous side: because Yajñadatta's attachment is accepted as a cause of the attachment arising in Devadatta's continuum; the English loses the subject and makes it generic.

fix.find: Because it is accepted that the cause of attachment arises within the mental continuum, your example is invalid.
fix.replace: Because Yajñadatta's attachment is accepted as a cause of the arising of attachment in Devadatta's continuum, your example fails.

errors.english: However, this lacks a proven basis and therefore you have no valid example.
errors.why: bsgrub par bya bas stong pa is the technical fault of an example 'empty of the probandum' (sādhyavikala), not 'lacking a proven basis'.

fix.find: However, this lacks a proven basis and therefore you have no valid example.
fix.replace: This example is empty of the property to be proved (sādhyavikala), and therefore you have no example.

errors.english: you are likewise refuting that
errors.why: The refutation is the commentator's own (kho bo ... 'gog pas): by refuting that Yajñadatta's attachment is the uncommon direct cause, his example is not empty of the probandum; the opponent does not refute anything here.

note: The dialectic of the drṣṭānta objection and reply is confused at its key points: the opponent's premise, the sādhyavikala fault and who refutes what.

errors.english: If mind [note: original: སེམས་, citta] were the self [note: original: བདག་, ātman], it could not be the object of the view of self.
errors.why: The point is that the past and future mind is not the object of the view of self (the following 'why' explains this by their ceasing and being unborn); the conditional 'if mind were the self' distorts the claim.

errors.english: to refute what harms the notion of a self
errors.why: bdag la gnod par byed pa is most likely an objection damaging 'us' (our no-self position, raised next about compassion without beings), not something that harms the notion of a self.

note: A clear rendering of the three-times analysis of mind and the plantain simile, with two loosely construed sentences.

errors.english: this object appearing from the primary word
errors.why: gtso bo is pradhāna, the Sāṃkhya primordial matter, the standard example of a subject whose existence is disputed; 'primary word' is meaningless here.

fix.find: this object appearing from the primary word
fix.replace: this object appearing from the word 'pradhāna' (primordial matter)

errors.english:
Some words would not have
Unreal objects.
errors.why: 'ga' zhig kyang with the negation means 'no word at all' would have a false object, not that 'some words' would not.

fix.find:
Some words would not have
Unreal objects.
fix.replace:
No words at all would have
Unreal objects.

errors.english: the cognition of both existence and non-existence
errors.why: The list has three members (cognitions of existence, of non-existence and of both), matching the three properties named next; the English collapses it to two.

note: The apoha argument and the summary verses are recognisable, but pradhāna is mistranslated and a universal negation in the verse is weakened.

errors.english: the Madhyamaka that teaches cessation
errors.why: In context ('they themselves are not nonexistent') 'gog par smra ba is a Madhyamaka of negation/denial (a nihilist label), not one teaching nirodha 'cessation'.

errors.english: then in that case, by that reasoning,
errors.why: The final 'rig' begins rig byed (the Vedas) on the next side ('then the Vedas too would be true'); 'by that reasoning' is invented from the broken word.

note: A good rendering of the Mahāyāna authenticity argument and the patriarch lineage, with a doubtful label and a mistranslated final syllable.
